page: Microsoft Azure E104ids_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 52 physical cores and 104 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 672.0 GB, yielding approximately 6.46 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. In addition to high memory capacity, the server bundles 4080 GB of fast local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage disks. Architectural extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic and vector instruction sets. The server contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation indicates strong parallel execution across multi-threaded computational workloads. Synthetic CPU evaluations place the multi-core score in the upper quartile with a stress-ng result of 100,881.58 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,965.0, while single-core metrics fall into the median range. Cryptographic acceleration is a notable strength, with PassMark encryption tests placing the platform in the top decile. Memory bandwidth testing demonstrates strong uncached large-block read throughput of 333.55 GB/sec and write throughput of 139.57 GB/sec. Application-level metrics reflect these memory and compute traits, generating 94.43 million Redis SET operations per second and high database operational throughput on synthetic tests.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the E104ids_v5 offers dense hardware consolidation by coupling a full host-isolated socket allocation with substantial memory and integrated high-capacity local SSDs. This reduces the latency and overhead associated with purely network-attached storage architectures for transactional workloads. The primary tradeoff lies in single-threaded velocity, which remains standard for this Intel generation. Consequently, the configuration is best matched to scale-up workloads where aggregate parallelism, memory capacity, and low-latency local disk scratch spaces are paramount, such as large relational databases, in-memory analytics clusters, high-concurrency Redis caching systems, and enterprise data warehousing.
description: Microsoft Azure E104ids_v5 is an isolated memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 104 dedicated vCPUs and 52 physical cores based on the 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 672 GB of total memory, allocating approximately 6.46 GB per core, alongside 4080 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Compute benchmarks reveal balanced single-core behavior alongside top-quartile multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, recording 333.55 GB/s in large-block read operations and top-decile cryptographic acceleration via hardware AVX-512, VAES, and SHA instructions. The high RAM capacity and local storage volume offer strong hardware density for resource-heavy operations without relying solely on remote network storage. While single-thread execution matches mainstream expectations, the server scales aggregate parallel throughput effectively. Azure E104ids_v5 is engineered for large-scale relational database engines, Redis caching arrays, in-memory data analytics, and enterprise data processing pipelines.
